note: Both sets read the five spanwise plots of Figure 2-4, but A binds more values correctly: chord ≈0.6 m and twist ≈−1.5 deg at r/R = 1.0, pitch-axis chord location 50% at the root, and prebend ≈0.3 m near r/R = 0.25, whereas B gives 1.5 m chord at the tip, 14 deg twist at the root, and 50% (and 100% over 0.0–0.1) relative thickness at the root even though the thickness curve is 100% only at r/R = 0. Both sets repeat claims and both wrongly place prebend 0.3 m at r/R = 0.4 (curve ≈0.1 m there); A additionally misplaces the zero-twist crossing at r/R ≈0.8 (it is ≈0.63) and the chord peak (5.3 m at 0.2 vs ≈5.8 m), while B overstates the 20% thickness range (0.7–1.0) and gives an inconsistent tip pitch-axis value. On balance A covers more of the important facts correctly with comparable error counts, so it is the better set.
